label: lem:trei.unu
title: \sc Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First, from the hypothesis, it is easily seen that the kernel $\Gamma$ is continuous on ${\mathcal D}_d^m \times {\mathcal D}_d^m$ and when $\Gamma(\varphi, \varphi) \ge 0,\ \varphi \in {\mathcal D}_d^m$, then $\Gamma$ is also positive definite. We shall attach an $m$-order $\mathscr{C}_{1}(H)$~-~valued distribution $C_{\Gamma}$ on $\mathbb{R}^{2d}$ as follows. Define first $C_{\Gamma}$ on the elementary tensors $\varphi\otimes\psi$ from ${\mathcal D}^{m}_{d}\otimes{\mathcal D}^{m}_{d}$ by
$C_{\Gamma}(\varphi\otimes\psi):= \Gamma(\varphi,\overline{\psi})$,
extend that by linearity, and then
by continuity to the whole ${\mathcal D}^{m}_{d}\widehat{\otimes}_{i}{\mathcal D}^{m}_{d}={\mathcal D}^{m}_{2d}$ preserving the notation $C_{\Gamma}$. \\
So $C_{\Gamma}\in\big({\mathcal D}^{m}_{2d}\big)'(\mathscr{C}_{1}(H))$, which, when $\Gamma$ is positive on the diagonal, will be a positive definite distribution kernel on ${\mathbb R}^d$. We shall refer to this as $C_{\Gamma}\in pd({\mathcal D}^{m}_{2d})'\big({\mathscr C}_{1}(H)\big)$.
head: environment

label: cor3.2
title: \sc Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor3.2}
For a given m.s.o. random distribution field $U\in\big({\mathcal D}^{m}_{d}\big)'({\mathscr H})$, the modular domain ${\mathscr H}_{U}$, respectively the measurements space $G_{U}$ will be isomorph to the ${\mathcal B}(H)$-module ${\mathscr H}_{\Gamma^{C_{U}}}$, respectively  the Hilbert space $G_{\Gamma^{C_{U}}}$ both reproduced by the $\mathscr{C}_{1}(H)$-valued kernel $\Gamma^{C_{U}}$, while the vector domain ${\mathscr H}_{(U)}$ of $U$ is isomorphic to the  Hilbert space reproduced by the complex valued kernel $\gamma^{C_{U}}$.
head: environment

title: \sc Corollary
body_md:
Given two m.s.o.r.d.f. $U$ and $V$ then $U$ is subordinate to $V$, iff for each fixed $\varphi \in {\mathcal D}_d$, the function $K_\varphi (\cdot)$ given by
\[
{\mathcal D}_d \ni \psi \mapsto C_{U,V} (\varphi \otimes \bar \psi) \in {\mathscr C}_1(H)
\]
lies in the ${\mathcal B}(H)$-module ${\mathscr H}_{\Gamma^{C_V}}$ and $\bigl[K_\varphi , K_\psi\bigr]_{{\mathscr H}_{\Gamma^{C_V}}} = C_U (\varphi \otimes \bar \psi)$.
head: environment

label: cor3.1
title: \sc Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor3.1}
For an $m$-order distribution kernel on ${\mathbb R}^d$, $C\in\big({\mathcal D}^{m}_{2d}\big)'(\mathscr{C}_{1}(H))$ the following statements are equivalent:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] $C\in pd\big({\mathcal D}^{m}_{2d}\big)'(\mathscr{C}_{1}(H))$; i.e. the operatorial kernel $\Gamma^{C}$ on ${\mathcal D}^{m}_{d}$ defined by
\(
\Gamma^{C}(\varphi,\psi):=C(\varphi\otimes\overline{\psi})\ (\varphi,\psi\in {\mathcal D}^{m}_{d})
\)
is positive definite.
\item[(ii)] The operatorial kernel $\Gamma^{C}$ is sesquilinear and positive (in the sense of positivity from ${\mathcal B}(H)$) on the diagonal of ${\mathcal D}^{m}_{d}\times{\mathcal D}^{m}_{d}$.
\item[(iii)] There is a m.s.o. random distribution field $U\in\big({\mathcal D}^{m}_{d}\big)'(\mathscr{H})$  such that $C=C_{U}$ (i.e. $C$ has a Kolmogorov type factorization).
\end{itemize}

title: \sc Corollary
body_md:
The m.s.o.r.d.f.'s $F, \ \xi^F,\ U^F$ as well as $\xi,\ U^\xi$ are simultaneously (operator) deterministic, (operator) nondeterministic or (operator) purely nondeterministic. Also the corresponding summands in the Wold decomposition are the same, i.e.
\[
(U^F)^{det} = U^{F^{det}},\quad (U^F)^p = U^{F^p},
\]
as well as
\[
(U^\xi)^{det} = U^{\xi^{det}} \quad (U^\xi)^p = U^{\xi^p}.
\]
